title: Agni, the witness
hook: Sita answers Rama, and calls the fire to witness her heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, the fire began with words: raja dharma, and the freedom to question it. Rama spoke coldly to Sita in front of everyone, and she wept. Today, her answer.
screen: `RAJA DHARMA, AND THE FREEDOM TO QUESTION IT.`

segments.voice: Sita wipes her tears. The crowd is silent: monkeys, bears, rakshasas, Lakshmana, Sugriva, Vibhishana, all waiting. And when she speaks, in Valmiki, her voice is steady. She doesn't beg. She doesn't apologize. She asks her husband a question: why are you talking to me the way a common man talks to a common woman? Then, point by point, in front of the same crowd that heard him, she answers everything he said.
screen: `SHE WIPES HER TEARS.` → `SHE DOESN'T BEG.` → `POINT BY POINT.`

segments.voice: What was in my power, she says, my heart, was always yours. When I was seized, my body was not in my power. Whose fault is that? And if you meant to give me up, why didn't you tell Hanuman when he found me? Then she asks Lakshmana to build a fire. Lakshmana, angry and pained, builds it at a sign from Rama. Sita walks around Rama in a circle of respect, folds her hands and calls on Agni, the god of fire: if my heart has never turned from Rama, protect me. And she walks into the flames. Why the fire? Because in Hindu tradition Agni is the witness. Offerings poured into a sacred fire pass through him to the gods, and at a Hindu wedding the couple walk around a fire and make their vows with Agni watching. Sita asks the witness of every vow to speak for her. The crowd cries out. Then, Valmiki says, the gods come down, and Brahma tells Rama who he really is: Vishnu himself. Agni rises out of the fire holding Sita, unharmed, her garlands untouched, and declares her pure. Rama answers that he never doubted her, but the world had to see it. Hindus read this scene in many ways. In some later tellings, like the Adhyatma Ramayana and Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, the real Sita was kept safe inside the fire all along, and only a shadow was taken to Lanka. Others hold to Valmiki's version and honor Sita's courage. And many readers today linger longest on her answer. Valmiki gave her those words. They're still there.
screen: `MY HEART WAS ALWAYS YOURS.` · `AGNI: THE WITNESS OF EVERY VOW.` · `AGNI GIVES HER BACK.` · `A SHADOW SITA, IN LATER TELLINGS.` · then, large: `VALMIKI GAVE HER THOSE WORDS.`

segments.voice: Many Hindu homes light a small lamp, a diya, at prayer time. If you have one, light it; or a candle; or just picture a small, steady flame. Name one promise you mean to keep, to someone or to yourself, and say it quietly to the flame, the way vows are made before Agni. If you don't pray, let the flame simply hold your attention while you breathe, and let the promise settle.
The fire. Sita answers Rama point by point, then calls on Agni, the witness of every vow, and Agni gives her back, unharmed.
Your line: the fire witnesses every vow. Sita called on it, and it answered. Tomorrow, the long way home begins. See you then.

howItsDone: At a Hindu wedding the couple walk around a sacred fire and make their vows with Agni as witness. The agni-parīkṣā, Sita's trial by fire, is retold and debated in homes, temples, classrooms and women's songs; different Ramayanas tell it differently.

fork.setup: at a Hindu wedding, the couple walk around a fire as they make their vows. by Sita's story, what is the fire doing there?
options: it's for light; old weddings ran late into the night.
it's Agni, the witness: the vows are made in front of him.
it burns away the couple's past so they start new.
fork.reveal: in Hindu ritual Agni is the witness, and the carrier of offerings to the gods. Sita called on that same witness for the truth of her heart.

original.note: Sanskrit agniparīkṣā: the trial by fire, from agni, fire, and parīkṣā, test or examination.

Agni.meaning: the god of fire, witness of every vow

Valmiki.meaning: the sage-poet who composed the Ramayana

Adhyatma Ramayana.meaning: a later Sanskrit Ramayana read in a devotional, spiritual way

Ramcharitmanas.meaning: Tulsidas's retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi
